slides.title: Simulink in the Aerospace Controls Lifecycle
slides.takeaway: A first-time user can move from an illustrative requirement to controlled desktop evidence without confusing training artifacts with certification approval.

slides.title: The executable model is the engineering hub
slides.takeaway: Requirements, control design, simulation, and verification meet around one inspectable model while retaining their separate responsibilities.

slides.title: Your first session: orient, execute, inspect, trace
slides.takeaway: The first session follows a repeatable sequence: start correctly, navigate the hierarchy, expose semantics, inspect data, and trace one result.

slides.title: MATLAB computes; Simulink exposes behavior
slides.takeaway: MATLAB configures, automates, and analyzes while Simulink makes dynamic data flow, state, timing, and interfaces visible.

slides.title: Start in the repository, then distinguish every action
slides.takeaway: Starting MATLAB R2023b in the repository and separating open, update, run, stop, build, and test actions makes every result reproducible and attributable.

slides.title: The toolstrip tells you where each action lives
slides.takeaway: Simulation, Debug, Modeling, Format, and Apps organize distinct actions and should not be treated as interchangeable paths to the same result.

slides.title: Turn model displays on—and off—for focus
slides.takeaway: Units, data types, dimensions, signal names, and logging or test-point badges expose model semantics without changing model behavior.

slides.title: The current job determines which model is top level
slides.takeaway: AircraftFeedbackControlLoop is the standalone closed-loop simulation, while the referenced architecture, child models, internal subsystems, and independent harness serve different jobs.

slides.title: AircraftFeedbackControlLoop closes the training loop
slides.takeaway: The standalone model connects pitch command, PI control, actuator dynamics, aircraft response, sensor lag, and feedback in one runnable desktop simulation.

slides.title: The Pitch Controller PI turns tracking error into demand
slides.takeaway: Proportional and discrete integral paths use controlled gains and a deterministic initial condition before their outputs are summed.

slides.title: Actuator Dynamics converts demand into position
slides.takeaway: The actuator subsystem makes command shaping and dynamic response explicit between controller demand and plant input.

slides.title: The longitudinal plant turns actuator motion into aircraft response
slides.takeaway: The simplified plant exposes the training relationship between actuator position, pitch-rate response, and pitch angle without claiming production-aircraft fidelity.

slides.title: Sensor Processing Lag makes measurement dynamics visible
slides.takeaway: The sensor subsystem separates true aircraft response from the filtered measurement returned to the controller.

slides.title: AutopilotModeLogic separates interfaces from mode behavior
slides.takeaway: The root model presents explicit pilot, validity, success, fault, disengage, and reset interfaces around its Stateflow chart.

slides.title: Stateflow guards OFF, ARMED, ENGAGED, and DEGRADED
slides.takeaway: Guarded transitions make discrete mode intent reviewable and provide direct boundary cases for verification.

slides.title: ReferencedFlightControlArchitecture is the integration top level
slides.takeaway: The integration model connects controlled interfaces across sensor processing, limiting, pitch control, and actuator-command references.

slides.title: SensorProcessingRef owns the referenced sensor contract
slides.takeaway: The referenced sensor component converts its defined input bus into reviewed processed-air-data outputs for downstream models.

slides.title: PitchRateLimiter is a separately managed component
slides.takeaway: The root component exposes a narrow command, mode, validity, limited-output, and active-status interface suitable for isolated verification.

slides.title: Pitch Rate Limiter Logic clamps magnitude and controls fallback
slides.takeaway: The implementation applies an inclusive magnitude clamp, zero fallback for invalid or non-normal operation, and explicit active-status logic—not slew-rate dynamics.

slides.title: PitchControllerRef defines the referenced controller boundary
slides.takeaway: The referenced controller packages its data contract and PI behavior independently from the standalone feedback-loop model.

slides.title: Pitch Rate PI implements the referenced control law
slides.takeaway: The internal subsystem preserves the proportional-plus-integral structure behind the referenced controller interface.

slides.title: ActuatorCommandRef owns final command limiting and status
slides.takeaway: The referenced actuator-command model makes command saturation, status, and downstream interface ownership visible at integration level.

slides.title: PitchRateLimiter_Harness isolates the unit under test
slides.takeaway: The independent harness supplies deterministic workspace stimuli to the referenced limiter and captures outputs without hiding pass/fail logic inside the model.

slides.title: Data Inspector makes one run inspectable without changing the model
slides.takeaway: The saved onboarding session shows command, response, error, actuator, and disturbance across three aligned plots for marker, cursor, timing, comparison, and export work.

slides.title: DO-178C defines objectives; DO-331 addresses model use
slides.takeaway: DO-178C is an accepted means of compliance, DO-331 supplements it for model-based work, and neither makes a Simulink model automatically compliant.

slides.title: Software levels scale rigor with consequence
slides.takeaway: System safety assessment assigns the software level, with Software Level A carrying the highest applicable rigor and independence objectives.

slides.title: Traceability turns artifacts into evidence
slides.takeaway: Bidirectional links explain both where every requirement is implemented and verified and why every model, test, result, and review artifact exists.

slides.title: The V-model pairs every definition with verification
slides.takeaway: Controlled baselines, ordered reviews, traceability, and designated independence remain necessary whether the lifecycle is agile, waterfall, or hybrid.

slides.title: Part 1 — plan, specify, develop, and test
slides.takeaway: Planning establishes lifecycle and tool roles before requirements, component development, harness design, deterministic setup, and focused verification begin.

slides.title: Part 2 — integrate, automate, investigate, prove
slides.takeaway: Integration, model update, automated execution, disciplined failure investigation, reruns, and retained evidence form a controlled verification loop.

slides.title: Illustrative requirements make the training chain explicit
slides.takeaway: System, software HLR, and software LLR or design statements define the limiter behavior under an explicit classroom-only scope.

slides.title: One limiter requirement traces to one executed result
slides.takeaway: PSYS-001 traces through SWHLR-001/PRL-001, SWLLR-001, Magnitude Clamp, the harness, and “Boundary above upper limit” to Iteration 8: 12.1 to 12.0 deg/s, zero error, PASS.

slides.title: The harness is one link in a controlled relative-file flow
slides.takeaway: FCS_Data.sldd feeds the harness and referenced limiter, while the MATLAB driver, traceability CSV, retained CSV/MAT results, and HTML/PNG report complete the chain.

slides.title: Reviewable models make intent obvious
slides.takeaway: Meaningful names, explicit contracts, consistent flow, focused hierarchy, and controlled reuse make model review a verification activity rather than a decoding exercise.

slides.title: Strong tests target boundaries, modes, failures, and timing
slides.takeaway: Nominal, exact-boundary, just-outside, invalid-mode, and 50 Hz timing cases expose the limiter behaviors most likely to fail.

slides.title: MATLAB tests preserve intent without a Test Manager file
slides.takeaway: Because Simulink Test is unavailable, the reviewable MATLAB suite executes 19 assessments and retains CSV, MAT, HTML, and PNG evidence without manufacturing a test-file .mldatx.

slides.title: Callbacks make execution deterministic
slides.takeaway: External setup, preload, post-load, execution, and cleanup functions establish reproducible context while leaving the verification oracle in the test driver.

slides.title: Jenkins makes verification repeatable
slides.takeaway: A pipeline orchestrates controlled MATLAB and Simulink operations and retains evidence, but a green stage is not certification approval.

slides.title: Classify the first meaningful failure
slides.takeaway: Reproduce first, distinguish environment, compile or interface, and functional failures, fix the root cause, add regression protection, and rerun controlled scope.

slides.title: HIL requires real controller hardware, real-time plant, and physical I/O
slides.takeaway: MIL, SIL, PIL, HIL, bench, and system-integration environments are distinct, and this training package performed desktop model execution rather than HIL.

slides.title: Pass criteria must be quantitative in every environment
slides.takeaway: Functional, timing, interface, fault-response, configuration, and retained-evidence criteria matter more than whether a plotted trace merely looks plausible.

slides.title: Your first week should produce one repeatable evidence chain
slides.takeaway: The current baseline records 8 of 8 models updated, 19 of 19 limiter assessments passed, and 24 of 24 required exported artifacts present, giving the learner a verified starting point for the next controlled change.
